title.narrative: Provision of life-saving multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance to crisis-affected rural communities in Baidoa

description.narrative: ltpgtThe communities in Baidoa have suffered the devastating consequences of prolonged droughts and floods that negatively impacted the livelihoods of rural communities, depleting their coping capacities and resilience. This has further strained their access to life-saving services, fueling displacement of rural communities to already swollen IDP camps. The limited resources worsen the vulnerability and exclusion of marginalized groups. Women and girls, who are mainly responsible for household chores face increased protection risks when fetching water or firewood. Persons with disabilities face access constraints due to non-inclusive infrastructure.lt/pgtltpgtIn response to this dire humanitarian situation, CESDO proposes a lifesaving, multi-sectoral project addressing the immediate and long-term WASH and food security needs of the hard-to-reach rural communities in Baidoa. While the project will respond to the priority needs identified by the communities through the CE partner and the ABC leadership, it is envisaged that through the installation of new water facilities and rehabilitating existing strategic water points, CESDO will ensure access to clean, safe water for these communities. This will improve public health outcomes by reducing water-related diseases such as acute water diarrhoea (AWD) and cholera. Communities will also have access to water for their livestock, reducing displacements triggered by water scarcity. By bringing services closer to the communities, protection risks faced by women, girls, persons with disabilities and minority groups when traveling long distance in search of services will be mitigated.lt/pgtltpgtThe project will ensure improved food security situation among target communities, particularly the most vulnerable and marginalized groups. CESDO will ensure vulnerability-based targeting and actively identify, engage and target groups most at risk of exclusion such as women, girls, the elderly, persons with disabilities and minority clans. The food security activities will contribute to improved access to diverse and nutritious foods and will target female-headed households, child-headed households, marginalized groups, pregnant and lactating women. This will consequently improve their nutrition and health outcomes, enhancing inter-sectoral synergies. Cash-based interventions will be prioritized, following comprehensive assessments of markets functionality and protection concerns.lt/pgtltpgtCESDO commits to non-discriminatory and impartial implementation of the project in-line with the Centrality of Protection, and adopts the recommendations from the 2024 CoP Report. To prevent the exclusion and denial of access to services, initial community mapping will be conducted in each location at the inception phase of the project. This will identify marginalized and excluded groups who will then be engaged throughout the project. They will be included in all the community-level committees, participating in the selection of beneficiaries and community-led project monitoring.lt/pgtltpgtCESDO is the co-chair of the Area Based Coordination (ABC) in Baidoa, and a long-term CCCM focal point in Baidoa rurals, particularly Berdale, and plans to leverage these platforms to ensure a coordinated response that ensures a comprehensive and complementary assistance to crisis-affected communities in Baidoa. Being the ABC co-chair, CESDO's contribution goes beyond the proposed project by effectively contribute to the selection of villages based on need and accessibility and identification of the priority humanitarian needs among the target communities.lt/pgtltpgtStrict measures will be taken to prevent duplication of assistance by identifying existing partners, regularly attending coordination meetings, and submitting the regular reports to the respective clusters and OCHA.lt/pgt
